ESV.1: And they brought in the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
ESV.2: And when David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD
ESV.3: and distributed to all Israel, both men and women, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat,  and a cake of raisins.
ESV.4: Then he appointed some of the Levites as ministers before the ark of the LORD, to invoke, to thank, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
ESV.5: Asaph was the chief, and second to him were Zechariah, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, who were to play harps and lyres; Asaph was to sound the cymbals,
ESV.6: and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were to blow trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God.
ESV.7: Then on that day David first appointed that thanksgiving be sung to the LORD by Asaph and his brothers.
ESV.8: Oh give thanks to the LORD; call upon his name; make known his deeds among the peoples!
ESV.9: Sing to him, sing praises to him; tell of all his wondrous works!
ESV.10: Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice!
ESV.11: Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his presence continually!
ESV.12: Remember the wondrous works that he has done, his miracles and the judgments he uttered,
ESV.13: O offspring of Israel his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones!
ESV.14: He is the LORD our God; his judgments are in all the earth.
ESV.15: Remember his covenant forever, the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,
ESV.16: the covenant that he made with Abraham, his sworn promise to Isaac,
ESV.17: which he confirmed to Jacob as a statute, to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
ESV.18: saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, as your portion for an inheritance.”
ESV.19: When you were few in number, of little account, and sojourners in it,
ESV.20: wandering from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people,
ESV.21: he allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings on their account,
ESV.22: saying, “Touch not my anointed ones, do my prophets no harm!”
ESV.23: Sing to the LORD, all the earth! Tell of his salvation from day to day.
ESV.24: Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples!
ESV.25: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised, and he is to be feared above all gods.
ESV.26: For all the gods of the peoples are worthless idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
ESV.27: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and joy are in his place.
ESV.28: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength!
ESV.29: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; bring an offering and come before him! Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness;
ESV.30: tremble before him, all the earth; yes, the world is established; it shall never be moved.
ESV.31: Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice, and let them say among the nations, “The LORD reigns!”
ESV.32: Let the sea roar, and all that fills it; let the field exult, and everything in it!
ESV.33: Then shall the trees of the forest sing for joy before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.
ESV.34: Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; for his steadfast love endures forever!
ESV.35: Say also: “Save us, O God of our salvation, and gather and deliver us from among the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.
ESV.36: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting!”  Then all the people said, “Amen!” and praised the LORD.
ESV.37: So David left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister regularly before the ark as each day required,
ESV.38: and also Obed-edom and his  sixty-eight brothers, while Obed-edom, the son of Jeduthun, and Hosah were to be gatekeepers.
ESV.39: And he left Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests before the tabernacle of the LORD in the high place that was at Gibeon
ESV.40: to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly morning and evening, to do all that is written in the Law of the LORD that he commanded Israel.
ESV.41: With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and expressly named to give thanks to the LORD, for his steadfast love endures forever.
ESV.42: Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for the music and instruments for sacred song. The sons of Jeduthun were appointed to the gate.
ESV.43: Then all the people departed each to his house, and David went home to bless his household.

NASB.1: And they brought in the ark of God and placed it inside the tent which David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
NASB.2: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
NASB.3: He distributed to everyone of Israel, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread and a portion [of meat] and a raisin cake.
NASB.4: He appointed some of the Levites [as] ministers before the ark of the LORD, even to celebrate and to thank and praise the LORD God of Israel:
NASB.5: Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, [then] Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom and Jeiel, with musical instruments, harps, lyres; also Asaph [played] loud-sounding cymbals,
NASB.6: and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests [blew] trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.
NASB.7: Then on that day David first assigned Asaph and his relatives to give thanks to the LORD.
NASB.8: Oh give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name; Make known His deeds among the peoples.
NASB.9: Sing to Him, sing praises to Him; Speak of all His wonders.
NASB.10: Glory in His holy name; Let the heart of those who seek the LORD be glad.
NASB.11: Seek the LORD and His strength; Seek His face continually.
NASB.12: Remember His wonderful deeds which He has done, His marvels and the judgments from His mouth,
NASB.13: O seed of Israel His servant, Sons of Jacob, His chosen ones!
NASB.14: He is the LORD our God; His judgments are in all the earth.
NASB.15: Remember His covenant forever, The word which He commanded to a thousand generations,
NASB.16: [The covenant] which He made with Abraham, And His oath to Isaac.
NASB.17: He also confirmed it to Jacob for a statute, To Israel as an everlasting covenant,
NASB.18: Saying, 'To you I will give the land of Canaan, As the portion of your inheritance.'
NASB.19: When they were only a few in number, Very few, and strangers in it,
NASB.20: And they wandered about from nation to nation, And from [one] kingdom to another people,
NASB.21: He permitted no man to oppress them, And He reproved kings for their sakes, [saying],
NASB.22: 'Do not touch My anointed ones, And do My prophets no harm.'
NASB.23: Sing to the LORD, all the earth; Proclaim good tidings of His salvation from day to day.
NASB.24: Tell of His glory among the nations, His wonderful deeds among all the peoples.
NASB.25: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; He also is to be feared above all gods.
NASB.26: For all the gods of the peoples are idols, But the LORD made the heavens.
NASB.27: Splendor and majesty are before Him, Strength and joy are in His place.
NASB.28: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples, Ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
NASB.29: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name; Bring an offering, and come before Him; Worship the LORD in holy array.
NASB.30: Tremble before Him, all the earth; Indeed, the world is firmly established, it will not be moved.
NASB.31: Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice; And let them say among the nations, 'The LORD reigns.'
NASB.32: Let the sea roar, and all it contains; Let the field exult, and all that is in it.
NASB.33: Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD; For He is coming to judge the earth.
NASB.34: O give thanks to the LORD, for [He is] good; For His lovingkindness is everlasting.
NASB.35: Then say, 'Save us, O God of our salvation, And gather us and deliver us from the nations, To give thanks to Your holy name, And glory in Your praise.'
NASB.36: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, From everlasting even to everlasting. Then all the people said, 'Amen,' and praised the LORD.
NASB.37: So he left Asaph and his relatives there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister before the ark continually, as every day's work required;
NASB.38: and Obed-edom with his 68 relatives; Obed-edom, also the son of Jeduthun, and Hosah as gatekeepers.
NASB.39: [He left] Zadok the priest and his relatives the priests before the tabernacle of the LORD in the high place which [was] at Gibeon,
NASB.40: to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering continually morning and evening, even according to all that is written in the law of the LORD, which He commanded Israel.
NASB.41: With them [were] Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest who were chosen, who were designated by name, to give thanks to the LORD, because His lovingkindness is everlasting.
NASB.42: And with them [were] Heman and Jeduthun [with] trumpets and cymbals for those who should sound aloud, and [with] instruments [for] the songs of God, and the sons of Jeduthun for the gate.
NASB.43: Then all the people departed each to his house, and David returned to bless his household.

WEB.1: They brought in God’s ark, and set it in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
WEB.2: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in Yahweh’s name.
WEB.3: He gave to everyone of Israel, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.
WEB.4: He appointed some of the Levites to minister before Yahweh’s ark, and to commemorate, to thank, and to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel:
WEB.5: Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, with stringed instruments and with harps; and Asaph with cymbals, sounding aloud;
WEB.6: with Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests with trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God.
WEB.7: Then on that day David first ordained to give thanks to Yahweh, by the hand of Asaph and his brothers.
WEB.8: Oh give thanks to Yahweh. Call on his name. Make what he has done known among the peoples.
WEB.9: Sing to him. Sing praises to him. Tell of all his marvelous works.
WEB.10: Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice.
WEB.11: Seek Yahweh and his strength. Seek his face forever more.
WEB.12: Remember his marvelous works that he has done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
WEB.13: you offspring  of Israel his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
WEB.14: He is Yahweh our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
WEB.15: Remember his covenant forever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
WEB.16: the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac.
WEB.17: He confirmed the same to Jacob for a statute, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
WEB.18: saying, “I will give you the land of Canaan, The lot of your inheritance,”
WEB.19: when you were but a few men in number, yes, very few, and foreigners were in it.
WEB.20: They went about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
WEB.21: He allowed no man to do them wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for their sakes,
WEB.22: “Don’t touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!”
WEB.23: Sing to Yahweh, all the earth! Display his salvation from day to day.
WEB.24: Declare his glory among the nations, and his marvelous works among all the peoples.
WEB.25: For great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised. He also is to be feared above all gods.
WEB.26: For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but Yahweh made the heavens.
WEB.27: Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and gladness are in his place.
WEB.28: Ascribe to Yahweh, you relatives of the peoples, ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength!
WEB.29: Ascribe to Yahweh the glory due to his name. Bring an offering, and come before him. Worship Yahweh in holy array.
WEB.30: Tremble before him, all the earth. The world also is established that it can’t be moved.
WEB.31: Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice! Let them say among the nations, “Yahweh reigns!”
WEB.32: Let the sea roar, and its fullness! Let the field exult, and all that is in it!
WEB.33: Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth.
WEB.34: Oh give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.
WEB.35: Say, “Save us, God of our salvation! Gather us together and deliver us from the nations, to give thanks to your holy name, to triumph in your praise.”
WEB.36: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting.  All the people said, “Amen,” and praised Yahweh.
WEB.37: So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of Yahweh’s covenant, to minister before the ark continually, as every day’s work required;
WEB.38: and Obed-Edom with their brothers, sixty-eight; Obed-Edom also the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be doorkeepers;
WEB.39: and Zadok the priest, and his brothers the priests, before Yahweh’s tabernacle in the high place that was at Gibeon,
WEB.40: to offer burnt offerings to Yahweh on the altar of burnt offering continually morning and evening, even according to all that is written in Yahweh’s law, which he commanded to Israel;
WEB.41: and with them Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest who were chosen, who were mentioned by name, to give thanks to Yahweh, because his loving kindness endures forever;
WEB.42: and with them Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and cymbals for those that should sound aloud, and with instruments for the songs of God; and the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate.
WEB.43: All the people departed, each man to his house; and David returned to bless his house.

NLT.1: They brought the Ark of God and placed it inside the special tent David had prepared for it. And they presented burnt offerings and peace offerings to God.
NLT.2: When he had finished his sacrifices, David blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
NLT.3: Then he gave to every man and woman in all Israel a loaf of bread, a cake of dates, and a cake of raisins.
NLT.4: David appointed the following Levites to lead the people in worship before the Ark of the LORD — to invoke his blessings, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
NLT.5: Asaph, the leader of this group, sounded the cymbals. Second to him was Zechariah, followed by Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. They played the harps and lyres.
NLT.6: The priests, Benaiah and Jahaziel, played the trumpets regularly before the Ark of God’s Covenant.
NLT.7: On that day David gave to Asaph and his fellow Levites this song of thanksgiving to the LORD:
NLT.8:
Give thanks to the LORD and proclaim his greatness.
Let the whole world know what he has done.
NLT.9:
Sing to him; yes, sing his praises.
Tell everyone about his wonderful deeds.
NLT.10:
Exult in his holy name;
rejoice, you who worship the LORD.
NLT.11:
Search for the LORD and for his strength;
continually seek him.
NLT.12:
Remember the wonders he has performed,
his miracles, and the rulings he has given,
NLT.13:
you children of his servant Israel,
you descendants of Jacob, his chosen ones.
NLT.14:
He is the LORD our God.
His justice is seen throughout the land.
NLT.15:
Remember his covenant forever —
the commitment he made to a thousand generations.
NLT.16:
This is the covenant he made with Abraham
and the oath he swore to Isaac.
NLT.17:
He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree,
and to the people of Israel as a never-ending covenant:
NLT.18:
“I will give you the land of Canaan
as your special possession.”
NLT.19:
He said this when you were few in number,
a tiny group of strangers in Canaan.
NLT.20:
They wandered from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another.
NLT.21:
Yet he did not let anyone oppress them.
He warned kings on their behalf:
NLT.22:
“Do not touch my chosen people,
and do not hurt my prophets.”
NLT.23:
Let the whole earth sing to the LORD!
Each day proclaim the good news that he saves.
NLT.24:
Publish his glorious deeds among the nations.
Tell everyone about the amazing things he does.
NLT.25:
Great is the LORD! He is most worthy of praise!
He is to be feared above all gods.
NLT.26:
The gods of other nations are mere idols,
but the LORD made the heavens!
NLT.27:
Honor and majesty surround him;
strength and joy fill his dwelling.
NLT.28:
O nations of the world, recognize the LORD,
recognize that the LORD is glorious and strong.
NLT.29:
Give to the LORD the glory he deserves!
Bring your offering and come into his presence.
Worship the LORD in all his holy splendor.
NLT.30:
Let all the earth tremble before him.
The world stands firm and cannot be shaken.
NLT.31:
Let the heavens be glad, and the earth rejoice!
Tell all the nations, “The LORD reigns!”
NLT.32:
Let the sea and everything in it shout his praise!
Let the fields and their crops burst out with joy!
NLT.33:
Let the trees of the forest sing for joy before the LORD,
for he is coming to judge the earth.
NLT.34:
Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good!
His faithful love endures forever.
NLT.35:
Cry out, “Save us, O God of our salvation!
Gather and rescue us from among the nations,
so we can thank your holy name
and rejoice and praise you.”
NLT.36:
Praise the LORD, the God of Israel,
who lives from everlasting to everlasting!
And all the people shouted “Amen!” and praised the LORD.
NLT.37: David arranged for Asaph and his fellow Levites to serve regularly before the Ark of the LORD’s Covenant, doing whatever needed to be done each day.
NLT.38: This group included Obed-edom (son of Jeduthun), Hosah, and sixty-eight other Levites as gatekeepers.
NLT.39: Meanwhile, David stationed Zadok the priest and his fellow priests at the Tabernacle of the LORD at the place of worship in Gibeon, where they continued to minister before the LORD.
NLT.40: They sacrificed the regular burnt offerings to the LORD each morning and evening on the altar set aside for that purpose, obeying everything written in the Law of the LORD, as he had commanded Israel.
NLT.41: David also appointed Heman, Jeduthun, and the others chosen by name to give thanks to the LORD, for “his faithful love endures forever.”
NLT.42: They used their trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments to accompany their songs of praise to God. And the sons of Jeduthun were appointed as gatekeepers.
NLT.43: Then all the people returned to their homes, and David turned and went home to bless his own family.

AMP.1: So they brought the ark of God and set it inside the tent which David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.

AMP.3: He distributed to everyone in Israel, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.
AMP.4: He appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD and to profess [God's name] and to thank and praise the LORD, the God of Israel:
AMP.5: Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel (Jaaziel), Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel with musical instruments, harps and lyres; also Asaph played loud-sounding cymbals;
AMP.6: and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests blew trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.

Sing to Him, sing praises to Him;

AMP.10:
Glory in His holy name;
Let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
AMP.11:
Seek the LORD and His strength;
Seek His face continually [longing to be in His presence].
AMP.12:
Remember [with gratitude] His marvelous deeds which He has done,

AMP.13:
O seed of Israel His servant,

AMP.14:
He is the LORD our God;
His judgments are in all the earth.
AMP.15:
Be mindful of His covenant forever,
The promise which He commanded and established to a thousand generations,
AMP.16:
The covenant which He made with Abraham,

AMP.17:
He confirmed it as a statute to Jacob,
And to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
AMP.18:
Saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan,

AMP.19:
When you were few in number,
Even a very few, and strangers in it,
AMP.20:
When they wandered from nation to nation,
And from one kingdom to another people,

He allowed no man to oppress or exploit them,

AMP.22:
"Do not touch My anointed ones,
And do My prophets no harm."
AMP.23:
Sing to the LORD, all the earth;
Proclaim the good news of His salvation from day to day.
AMP.24:
Declare His glory among the nations,
His marvelous works among all peoples.
AMP.25:
For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised;
He is also to be feared [with awe-filled reverence] above all gods.
AMP.26:
For all the gods of the peoples are [lifeless] idols,

AMP.27:
Splendor and majesty are [found] in His presence;

AMP.28:
Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples,

Tremble [reverently] before Him, all the earth;

Let the sea roar, and all the things that fill it;

AMP.33:
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD;

AMP.34:
O give thanks to the LORD, for He is good;

AMP.35:
Then say, "Save us, O God of our salvation;

MSG.1: They brought the Chest of God and placed it right in the center of the tent that David had pitched for it; then they worshiped by presenting burnt offerings and peace offerings to God.
MSG.2: When David had completed the offerings of worship, he blessed the people in the name of God.
MSG.3: Then he passed around to every one there, men and women alike, a loaf of bread, a slice of barbecue, and a raisin cake.
MSG.4: Then David assigned some of the Levites to the Chest of God to lead worship—to intercede, give thanks, and praise the God of Israel.
MSG.5: Asaph was in charge; under him were Zechariah, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, who played the musical instruments. Asaph was on percussion.
MSG.6: The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blew the trumpets before the Chest of the Covenant of God at set times through the day.
MSG.7: That was the day that David inaugurated regular worship of praise to God, led by Asaph and his company.
MSG.8:
Thank God! Call out his Name!
Tell the whole world who he is and what he's done!
MSG.9:
Sing to him! Play songs for him!
Broadcast all his wonders!
MSG.10:
Revel in his holy Name,
God-seekers, be jubilant!
MSG.11:
Study God and his strength,
seek his presence day and night;
MSG.12:
Remember all the wonders he performed,
the miracles and judgments that came out of his mouth.
MSG.13:
Seed of Israel his servant!
Children of Jacob, his first choice!
MSG.14:
He is God, our God;
wherever you go you come on his judgments and decisions.
MSG.15:
He keeps his commitments across thousands
of generations, the covenant he commanded,
MSG.16:
The same one he made with Abraham,
the very one he swore to Isaac;
MSG.17:
He posted it in big block letters to Jacob,
this eternal covenant with Israel:
MSG.18:
"I give you the land of Canaan,
this is your inheritance;
MSG.19:
Even though you're not much to look at,
a few straggling strangers."
MSG.20:
They wandered from country to country,
camped out in one kingdom after another;
MSG.21:
But he didn't let anyone push them around,
he stood up for them against bully-kings:
MSG.22:
"Don't you dare touch my anointed ones,
don't lay a hand on my prophets."
MSG.23:
Sing to God, everyone and everything!
Get out his salvation news every day!
MSG.24:
Publish his glory among the godless nations,
his wonders to all races and religions.
MSG.25:
And why? Because God is great—well worth praising!
No god or goddess comes close in honor.
MSG.26:
All the popular gods are stuff and nonsense,
but God made the cosmos!
MSG.27:
Splendor and majesty flow out of him,
strength and joy fill his place.
MSG.28:
Shout Bravo! to God, families of the peoples,
in awe of the Glory, in awe of the Strength: Bravo!
MSG.29:
Shout Bravo! to his famous Name,
lift high an offering and enter his presence!
Stand resplendent in his robes of holiness!
MSG.30:
God is serious business, take him seriously;
he's put the earth in place and it's not moving.
MSG.31:
So let heaven rejoice, let earth be jubilant,
and pass the word among the nations, "God reigns!"
MSG.32:
Let Ocean, all teeming with life, bellow,
let Field and all its creatures shake the rafters;
MSG.33:
Then the trees in the forest will add their applause
to all who are pleased and present before God
—he's on his way to set things right!
MSG.34:
Give thanks to God—he is good
and his love never quits.
MSG.35:
Say, "Save us, Savior God,
round us up and get us out of these godless places,

and bask in your life of praise."
MSG.36:
Blessed be God, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.

NIV.14:
He is the Lord our God;
his judgments are in all the earth.
NIV.15:
He remembers his covenant forever,
the word he commanded, for a thousand generations,
NIV.16:
the covenant he made with Abraham,
the oath he swore to Isaac.
NIV.17:
He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree,
to Israel as an everlasting covenant:
NIV.18:
“To you I will give the land of Canaan
as the portion you will inherit.”
NIV.19:
When they were but few in number,
few indeed, and strangers in it,
NIV.20:
they wandered from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another.
NIV.21:
He allowed no man to oppress them;
for their sake he rebuked kings:
NIV.22:
“Do not touch my anointed ones;
do my prophets no harm.”
NIV.23:
Sing to the Lord, all the earth;
proclaim his salvation day after day.
NIV.24:
Declare his glory among the nations,
his marvelous deeds among all peoples.
NIV.25:
For great is the Lord and most worthy of praise;
he is to be feared above all gods.
NIV.26:
For all the gods of the nations are idols,
but the Lord made the heavens.
NIV.27:
Splendor and majesty are before him;
strength and joy in his dwelling place.
NIV.28:
Ascribe to the Lord, O families of nations,
ascribe to the Lord glory and strength,
NIV.29:
ascribe to the Lord the glory due his name.
Bring an offering and come before him;
worship the Lord in the splendor of his holiness.
NIV.30:
Tremble before him, all the earth!
The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.
NIV.31:
Let the heavens rejoice, let the earth be glad;
let them say among the nations, “The Lord reigns!”
NIV.32:
Let the sea resound, and all that is in it;
let the fields be jubilant, and everything in them!
NIV.33:
Then the trees of the forest will sing,
they will sing for joy before the Lord,
for he comes to judge the earth.
NIV.34:
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good;
his love endures forever.
NIV.35:
Cry out, “Save us, O God our Savior;
gather us and deliver us from the nations,
that we may give thanks to your holy name,
that we may glory in your praise.”
NIV.36:
Praise be to the Lord, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.
Then all the people said “Amen” and “Praise the Lord.”
NIV.37: David left Asaph and his associates before the ark of the covenant of the Lord to minister there regularly, according to each day’s requirements.
NIV.38: He also left Obed-Edom and his sixty-eight associates to minister with them. Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun, and also Hosah, were gatekeepers.
NIV.39: David left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the Lord at the high place in Gibeon
NIV.40: to present burnt offerings to the Lord on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, in accordance with everything written in the Law of the Lord, which he had given Israel.
NIV.41: With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the Lord, “for his love endures forever.”
NIV.42: Heman and Jeduthun were responsible for the sounding of the trumpets and cymbals and for the playing of the other instruments for sacred song. The sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate.
NIV.43: Then all the people left, each for his own home, and David returned home to bless his family.

NRSVCE.1: They brought in the ark of God, and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it; and they offered burnt offerings and offerings of well-being before God.
NRSVCE.2: When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the offerings of well-being, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD;
NRSVCE.3: and he distributed to every person in Israel — man and woman alike — to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.
NRSVCE.4: He appointed certain of the Levites as ministers before the ark of the LORD, to invoke, to thank, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
NRSVCE.5: Asaph was the chief, and second to him Zechariah, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with harps and lyres; Asaph was to sound the cymbals,
NRSVCE.6: and the priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to blow trumpets regularly, before the ark of the covenant of God.
NRSVCE.7: Then on that day David first appointed the singing of praises to the LORD by Asaph and his kindred.
NRSVCE.8:
O give thanks to the LORD, call on his name,
make known his deeds among the peoples.
NRSVCE.9:
Sing to him, sing praises to him,
tell of all his wonderful works.
NRSVCE.10:
Glory in his holy name;
let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
NRSVCE.11:
Seek the LORD and his strength,
seek his presence continually.
NRSVCE.12:
Remember the wonderful works he has done,
his miracles, and the judgments he uttered,
NRSVCE.13:
O offspring of his servant Israel,
children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
NRSVCE.14:
He is the LORD our God;
his judgments are in all the earth.
NRSVCE.15:
Remember his covenant forever,
the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,
NRSVCE.16:
the covenant that he made with Abraham,
his sworn promise to Isaac,
NRSVCE.17:
which he confirmed to Jacob as a statute,
to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
NRSVCE.18:
saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan
as your portion for an inheritance.”
NRSVCE.19:
When they were few in number,
of little account, and strangers in the land,
NRSVCE.20:
wandering from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people,
NRSVCE.21:
he allowed no one to oppress them;
he rebuked kings on their account,
NRSVCE.22:
saying, “Do not touch my anointed ones;
do my prophets no harm.”
NRSVCE.23:
Sing to the LORD, all the earth.
Tell of his salvation from day to day.
NRSVCE.24:
Declare his glory among the nations,
his marvelous works among all the peoples.
NRSVCE.25:
For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised;
he is to be revered above all gods.
NRSVCE.26:
For all the gods of the peoples are idols,
but the LORD made the heavens.
NRSVCE.27:
Honor and majesty are before him;
strength and joy are in his place.
NRSVCE.28:
Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples,
ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
NRSVCE.29:
Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name;
bring an offering, and come before him.
Worship the LORD in holy splendor;
NRSVCE.30:
tremble before him, all the earth.
The world is firmly established; it shall never be moved.
NRSVCE.31:
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice,
and let them say among the nations, “The LORD is king!”
NRSVCE.32:
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
let the field exult, and everything in it.
NRSVCE.33:
Then shall the trees of the forest sing for joy
before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.
NRSVCE.34:
O give thanks to the LORD, for he is good;
for his steadfast love endures forever.
NRSVCE.35:
Say also: “Save us, O God of our salvation,
and gather and rescue us from among the nations,
that we may give thanks to your holy name,
and glory in your praise.
NRSVCE.36:
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.”
Then all the people said “Amen!” and praised the LORD.
NRSVCE.37: David left Asaph and his kinsfolk there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister regularly before the ark as each day required,
NRSVCE.38: and also Obed-edom and his sixty-eight kinsfolk; while Obed-edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were to be gatekeepers.
NRSVCE.39: And he left the priest Zadok and his kindred the priests before the tabernacle of the LORD in the high place that was at Gibeon,
NRSVCE.40: to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, according to all that is written in the law of the LORD that he commanded Israel.
NRSVCE.41: With them were Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest of those chosen and expressly named to render thanks to the LORD, for his steadfast love endures forever.
NRSVCE.42: Heman and Jeduthun had with them trumpets and cymbals for the music, and instruments for sacred song. The sons of Jeduthun were appointed to the gate.
NRSVCE.43: Then all the people departed to their homes, and David went home to bless his household.

NET.1: They brought the ark of God and put it in the middle of the tent David had pitched for it. Then they offered burnt sacrifices and peace offerings before God.
NET.2: When David finished offering burnt sacrifices and peace offerings, he pronounced a blessing over the people in the LORD’s name.
NET.3: He then handed out to each Israelite man and woman a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake.
NET.4: He appointed some of the Levites to serve before the ark of the LORD, to offer prayers, songs of thanks, and hymns to the LORD God of Israel.
NET.5: Asaph was the leader and Zechariah second in command, followed by Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel. They were to play stringed instruments; Asaph was to sound the cymbals;
NET.6: and the priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to blow trumpets regularly before the ark of God’s covenant.
NET.7: That day David first gave to Asaph and his colleagues this song of thanks to the LORD:
NET.8: Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name! Make known his accomplishments among the nations!
NET.9: Sing to him! Make music to him! Tell about all his miraculous deeds!
NET.10: Boast about his holy name! Let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice!
NET.11: Seek the LORD and the strength he gives! Seek his presence continually!
NET.12: Recall the miraculous deeds he performed, his mighty acts and the judgments he decreed,
NET.13: O children of Israel, God’s servant, you descendants of Jacob, God’s chosen ones!
NET.14: He is the LORD our God; he carries out judgment throughout the earth.
NET.15: Remember continually his covenantal decree, the promise he made to a thousand generations —
NET.16: the promise he made to Abraham, the promise he made by oath to Isaac!
NET.17: He gave it to Jacob as a decree, to Israel as a lasting promise,
NET.18: saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan as the portion of your inheritance.”
NET.19: When they were few in number, just a very few, and foreign residents within it,
NET.20: they wandered from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another.
NET.21: He let no one oppress them, he disciplined kings for their sake,
NET.22: saying, “Don’t touch my anointed ones! Don’t harm my prophets!”
NET.23: Sing to the LORD, all the earth! Announce every day how he delivers!
NET.24: Tell the nations about his splendor, tell all the nations about his miraculous deeds!
NET.25: For the LORD is great and certainly worthy of praise, he is more awesome than all gods.
NET.26: For all the gods of the nations are worthless, but the LORD made the heavens.
NET.27: Majestic splendor emanates from him, he is the source of strength and joy.
NET.28: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the nations, ascribe to the LORD splendor and strength!
NET.29: Ascribe to the LORD the splendor he deserves! Bring an offering and enter his presence! Worship the LORD in holy attire!
NET.30: Tremble before him, all the earth! The world is established, it cannot be moved.
NET.31: Let the heavens rejoice, and the earth be happy! Let the nations say, ‘The LORD reigns!’
NET.32: Let the sea and everything in it shout! Let the fields and everything in them celebrate!
NET.33: Then let the trees of the forest shout with joy before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth!
NET.34: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good and his loyal love endures.
NET.35: Say this prayer: “Deliver us, O God who delivers us! Gather us! Rescue us from the nations! Then we will give thanks to your holy name, and boast about your praiseworthy deeds.”
NET.36: May the LORD God of Israel be praised, in the future and forevermore. Then all the people said, “We agree! Praise the LORD!”
NET.37: David left Asaph and his colleagues there before the ark of the LORD’s covenant to serve before the ark regularly and fulfill each day’s requirements,
NET.38: including Obed-Edom and sixty-eight colleagues. Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.
NET.39: Zadok the priest and his fellow priests served before the LORD’s tabernacle at the worship center in Gibeon,
NET.40: regularly offering burnt sacrifices to the LORD on the altar for burnt sacrifice, morning and evening, according to what is prescribed in the law of the LORD which he charged Israel to observe.
NET.41: Joining them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the rest of those chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD. (For his loyal love endures!)
NET.42: Heman and Jeduthun were in charge of the music, including the trumpets, cymbals, and the other musical instruments used in praising God. The sons of Jeduthun guarded the entrance.
NET.43: Then all the people returned to their homes, and David went to pronounce a blessing on his family.
